label: Zen Library
Downloads, media, history, easels, spaces and boosts in one panel. Open it with Alt+Shift+B, or from the Library button.
Toolbar button
Show the Library button in the toolbar

The button is an ordinary toolbar widget: right-click the toolbar and choose Customize Toolbar to drag it anywhere, and it stays where you put it. Untick the box above to hide it, or tick it again to put it back beside the workspace indicator.
Shortcuts

Zen Library takes over Ctrl+H and Ctrl+J so they open its own History and Downloads sections instead of Firefox's panels. Turn either off to hand the key back — to the native panel, and to web pages that bind it.
Ctrl+H (Cmd+H on macOS) opens the Library's History
Ctrl+J (Cmd+J on macOS) opens the Library's Downloads
Downloads
Also show files from the Downloads folder

When enabled, the Downloads section lazily scans your Downloads folder and adds top-level files or folders Firefox no longer has in its download history. Folder contents are not shown separately. Changes apply immediately while the panel is open.
Animation
Defaults match Zen's native library (280 ms, cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)). Lower the duration or pick Snappy for a quicker feel. Applies the next time the panel opens.

Compatibility
Advanced Tab Groups integration

With the Advanced Tab Groups mod installed, the Library renders its tab groups in the Spaces section itself instead of letting the mod patch in its own rows: groups expand and collapse like folders (the active tab stays visible under a collapsed header), can be dragged to reorder, nested into other groups, moved between spaces, and turned into a folder by dropping them in the pinned area — a folder dropped among the unpinned tabs becomes a tab group. Also keeps the mod's tab-strip hooks from rebuilding the panel on every tab move or close. Off: the mod's own Library rendering is used. Restart Zen after changing.
